ledger.claim: The free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and the fee is the consideration the rider paid for that period. The driver's own trace shows a single in-geofence stationary run lasting 57 seconds, from 14:22:40 to 14:23:37 — a shortfall of 123 seconds against the 180 seconds required. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages; the shortfall is strict-liability arithmetic, so no finding about the rider's conduct is needed to dispose of the charge.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) measures the continuous dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver's arrival tap, and limb (c) is the limb on which this charge breaks. The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 14:22:40 and terminated the trip at 14:23:41 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW; the free-wait timer itself ran only from 14:22:42 to the cancellation. On the trace-derived clock the dwell is 57 seconds and on the platform's own timer 59 seconds — roughly a third of the 180-second minimum — so limb (c) fails and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

The rider did everything the platform asks of a waiting rider and was met with silence. She sent 'coming out now' at 14:23:40, inside the waiting window and after the driver's arrival marker, telling the driver she was on her way out to the pickup point — a locating/coordinating message under POL-NS-04(a). The chat log holds exactly one message and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so the driver never replied within the 120 seconds of limb (b) and never placed an in-app voice call before terminating. Her own track places her device inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius on all 19 qualifying fixes, never more than about 7.4 m from the pin, so limb (c) is affirmatively satisfied by admissible fixes rather than undecidable, POL-NS-11 has nothing to operate on, and the clause exonerates the rider with the fee refunded in full and no driver compensation payable.

EV-ADVIS-02754-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 in this window. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory is present and populated, so the driver cannot use the absent advisory to extend or accumulate his dwell, and its absence is itself citable under POL-GEN-02. Independently, the trace records run_count 1 and a single 57-second interval beginning at the arrival fix, so there is no second interval for limb (i) to add to the first and nothing turns on the advisory either way.

The driver's counterstatement asks the tribunal to 'check the profile' for a history of no-shows. POL-GEN-01 forecloses that route: prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only, never a ground of decision, and the trailing-window field that the policy does name, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, stands at 1 — below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires before profile history can even escalate, let alone decide. No profile field on either party can establish anything about this trip; the trip is decided on the driver's own trace, which shows the shortfall.

ledger.claim: No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is engaged, so the fee should be refunded now rather than held on review. Every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0: the 'arrived' event at 14:22:40 matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix to the second (no clock skew approaching POL-NS-08's 90-second limb (a)), the trace runs at 100 percent coverage with max_gap_sec 0.0 over 69 fixes (no limb (b) gap), the single chat message matches chat_message_count 1 with no msg_id break (no limb (c) defect), and the 4.50 cancellation-fee line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd (no limb (d) defect). The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check cannot trip on 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 58 completed trips, and both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, so the deciding facts rest on clean evidence and confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor.

The platform's own arrival and wait-timer telemetry cannot be used to treat the waiting period as served. POL-NS-12 is confined to trips whose arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO; this trip's marker is BUTTON (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker), and a driver-pressed marker remains subject to POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-05. The exported trace therefore governs, and it stops the driver's in-geofence dwell at 57 seconds — not the 180 seconds the fee requires.

The rider filed this dispute, so the outcome that leaves her not carrying the disputed charge is a refund of the cancellation-fee line: the fare breakdown shows SGD 4.50 charged at 14:23:58 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND returns the whole contested amount of SGD 4.50 to the filing party, and the monetary effect is well below the execution threshold, so the refund is executed on issue rather than held.

The driver's arrival is established on measured evidence, not on his own tap: EV-TRIP-02754 logs the driver_arrived event at 2026-09-16T14:22:40+08:00, satisfying limb (a) of POL-NS-01, and EV-GPS-02754 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius with 7 qualifying fixes whose first in-geofence fix falls in that same 14:22:40 second and whose nearest approach to the pin is 1.13 m. That is at least 3 consecutive in-radius fixes under the 25 m accuracy filter, so the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied and limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-01 both hold.

The arrival marker is not a false marker, and no false-arrival referral should be recorded against this driver. At the 14:22:40 marker the driver's nearest fix is 1.13 m from the pickup pin, far inside the more-than-300 m distance trigger of POL-NS-05, and the in-geofence run is a held position whose trace speed is 0.0 kph against the clause's 15 kph motion trigger - nothing in EV-GPS-02754 shows the driver in motion at the marker. The marker therefore stands and the waiting clock runs from the GPS-confirmed arrival as EV-TRIP-02754 records it, so POL-NS-05(ii) and (iii) have nothing to refer.

POL-NS-03 has no application here and no wrong-face-of-the-venue finding is available: that clause governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, whereas the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m STANDARD radius at the registered pickup point itself (pickup.venue_id VEN-SERANGOON-AVE3, registered_pickup_points 1). The driver reached the pin at Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3, so this is not a mislocation case and no pin-ambiguity goodwill falls to be allocated.

The termination limb and the arithmetic are clean. No boarding event appears in EV-TRIP-02754 and the trip was terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises. The single cancellation-fee line in EV-FARE-02754 is SGD 4.50, exactly the net figure platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd states for this trip, with payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and no waiting-time line at all. There is accordingly no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the only sum in issue is that fee line of SGD 4.50.

The rider's single message does not open POL-NS-04. 'coming out now', sent 14:23:40 and delivered one second before the termination, names no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for no position and does not say the vehicle could not be seen, so it is not a locating or coordinating message within limb (a). EV-GPS-02754 shows the rider's device within about 7.4 m of the pickup point from 14:21:40 onward, so the record is of a rider who was at the pickup point through the wait and did not present herself, not of a driver who ignored an attempt to coordinate; no coordination-failure finding should be recorded against this driver.

Any rider argument built on the cancellation grace fails on the record: the cancellation was the driver's (cancelled_by DRIVER, status CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER) at 14:23:41, more than ten minutes after accepted_at 14:13:12, so the 180 second grace in POL-NS-10(a) cannot make this fee non-chargeable, and no waiting-time fee was charged for POL-NS-10(d) or (e) to refund.

I do not argue the waiting limb up, because the driver's own numbers will not carry it: the longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run in EV-GPS-02754 is 57 seconds, from 14:22:40 to 14:23:37, against the 180 seconds of free waiting time in force under POL-NS-01(c) (platform_policy.free_wait_sec 180), a shortfall of 123 seconds. The platform's own clock agrees - its wait timer started at 14:22:42 and the termination fell at 14:23:41. The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) is not open either: the trace shows one in-geofence interval with no second interval to sum, and the traffic_advisory it would require, EV-ADVIS-02754-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, no payload), so I assert no kerb restriction and rest on no advisory. That shortfall confines the remedy to the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 under POL-NS-06; what the record does not contain is a false marker, a mislocated arrival or a defective fare line for POL-NS-05, POL-NS-03 or POL-NS-08 to record.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling for the rider: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee is refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Both parties accept, and the record shows, that the driver really did reach the pickup point. EV-TRIP-02754 logs the 'arrived' event at 2026-09-16T14:22:40+08:00, and EV-GPS-02754 puts him 1.13 m from the pin, stationary at 0.0 km/h at that moment, with 7 qualifying in-radius fixes. The arrival marker is therefore genuine: POL-NS-05 records no false arrival and no false-arrival referral, and POL-NS-03 has no application (his stationary fixes are inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so this is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case).

The fee nevertheless fails on the waiting period. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position for the free waiting period in force, which is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). He cancelled at 14:23:41, only 61 seconds after the 14:22:40 marker, and the longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run in EV-GPS-02754 is 57 seconds (14:22:40 to 14:23:37) against the 180 seconds required — a shortfall of 123 seconds. The platform's own wait timer, started at 14:22:42 and cut off by the cancellation, ran to about 59 seconds. POL-NS-06 therefore governs: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. The driver has no accumulation route — EV-ADVIS-02754-01 is MISSING with no advisory payload, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run, and the trace shows a single in-geofence interval in any event. Because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full, POL-NS-07 gives the driver nothing, and no compensation is payable.

On the rider's side, whether 'coming out now' (sent 14:23:40) is a locating or coordinating message under POL-NS-04(a) does not affect the money: the same outcome — full refund of the SGD 4.50 and no driver compensation — already follows from POL-NS-06, so the point need not be resolved. Her device was within about 7.4 m of the pin throughout, consistent with that outcome.

The driver's counterstatement asks the tribunal to check the rider's history of no-shows. That cannot decide anything here: under POL-GEN-01 rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is context only, and the trailing-window counter the policy does name, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, stands at 1, below the 3 required.

No escalation is engaged. Every artifact relied on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap on the deciding dwell fact is 1.0, and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 58 completed trips), and both counterparty-dispute counters are 0. The refund of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
